# Publishing salted click records to Kafka

> Each ad click publishes to Kafka with a random salt (0–9) appended to the campaign ID key, spreading viral traffic across 10 partitions to avoid overloading one.

_Part of [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md)_

In the `click` handler of `ads.service.ts`, after verifying the token and checking for fraud, a [`ClickRecord`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) is sent to the `ads.clicks` Kafka topic with a salted key. The key combines the campaign ID with a random integer from 0–9: `campaignId#salt`. This means 10,000 clicks/sec on one viral ad distributes evenly across partitions instead of hammering one. [Click verification and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) produces both valid and invalid records; [downstream aggregators](exactly-once-transaction.md) read all 10 salted keys and merge them back by campaign.

**Look at:** [`click` in ads.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/ads.service.ts#L9)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| queue | `ads.clicks` | Every click (valid or invalid) publishes a [`ClickRecord`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) containing `click_id`, `campaign_id`, `shop_id`, timestamp, `ip_hash`, and a valid flag (0 or 1); downstream jobs aggregate and bill from this topic. |
| cache | `adclick:ip:HASH:MINUTE (Redis)` | Checked during click handling to enforce the 20-clicks-per-minute burst limit that determines if a click is valid. |
| cache | `adspend:CAMPAIGN_ID:DATE (Redis)` | Incremented by cost-per-click when a valid click publishes; checked to enforce daily spend budgets. |

## Also relies on

- [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md): Token verification and burst checking produce the click record and valid flag before publishing to Kafka.

## Watch out

- Changing [`HOT_KEY_SALTS`](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md) (the 0–9 range) requires updating all consumers, or clicks fall into unread partitions.
- The valid field is 0 or 1, not a boolean; JSON and SQL parsers may need explicit type handling.
- Consumers must read all 10 partitions of `ads.clicks` and merge by campaign; reading just one partition will miss 90% of clicks.
- Invalid clicks (burst overages and duplicates) still publish to Kafka; you must filter on valid=1 when aggregating billable traffic.
